prompt:
A loaded lorry of total mass 1.6 x 10^4 kg climbs a straight hill inclined at angle theta to the horizontal, where sin theta = 0.040 (a 1 in 25 slope).
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Heavy lorry of mass 1.6 x 10^4 kg travelling up an inclined road at angle theta to the horizontal. Driving force F acts up the slope. Constant resistive force R = 1800 N acts down the slope. Downward weight W = mg has components mg sin theta down the incline and mg cos theta into the incline.]
The lorry travels at a constant speed of 15 m s^-1 up the incline. A constant resistive force of 1800 N opposes the motion. Take g = 9.81 m s^-2.
(a) Calculate the component of the weight acting parallel to the slope down the incline. [1]
(b) Calculate the driving force required to maintain the constant speed of 15 m s^-1 up the incline. [2]
(c) Calculate the useful mechanical power output delivered by the engine. [1]
(d) The lorry engine has an efficiency of 30%. Calculate the rate of chemical energy consumption from the fuel (the input power). [1]
(e) The lorry now travels down the same slope at the same constant speed of 15 m s^-1 with the same resistive force of 1800 N. Explain, with a calculation, whether the engine must supply a driving force or whether braking is required. [1]

mark_scheme.criterion: Calculates downhill weight component: W_parallel = mg sin theta = 1.6 * 10^4 * 9.81 * 0.040 = 6280 N (accept 6300 N or 6278 N).
States equilibrium equation up slope: F_drive = R + mg sin theta = 1800 + 6278.
Calculates forward driving force = 8080 N (accept 8100 N).
Calculates useful power output: P = Fv = 8078 * 15 = 121 000 W (accept 120 kW or 121 kW).
Applies efficiency to find fuel rate: P_in = 121 176 / 0.30 = 404 000 W (accept 4.0 * 10^5 W or 404 kW).
Compares downhill weight (6280 N) with resistance (1800 N) to show net downhill force of 4480 N, concluding braking is required.

part_enrichment.guidance: Multiply total mass by g and sin theta: 16 000 * 9.81 * 0.040.
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Using cos theta instead of sin theta.

marking_points.criterion: Sets up force balance up slope: F_drive = resistance + weight component.

part_enrichment.guidance: Constant velocity requires resultant force along slope to be zero.
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Subtracting resistance instead of adding it.

part_enrichment.guidance: Multiply total driving force by speed.

marking_points.criterion: Shows downhill weight component 6280 N > resistance 1800 N, so braking of 4480 N is required.

part_enrichment.guidance: When travelling downhill, gravity acts in direction of motion.
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Assuming engine must always provide forward thrust to maintain speed.

hints: In (a), weight component down slope is mg sin theta.
In (b), driving force must overcome both gravity and resistance.
In (e), compare downhill weight component with the opposing resistance.
solution:
(a) W_parallel = mg sin theta = 1.6 * 10^4 * 9.81 * 0.040 = 6278.4 N approx 6.3 kN.
(b) F_drive = 1800 + 6278.4 = 8078.4 N approx 8.1 kN.
(c) P_useful = 8078.4 * 15 = 121 176 W approx 121 kW.
(d) P_fuel = 121 176 / 0.30 = 403 920 W approx 404 kW.
(e) Moving downhill, the component of weight down the incline is 6278 N forward. The resistance is 1800 N backward. Since 6278 N > 1800 N, the vehicle would accelerate unless a braking force of 6278 - 1800 = 4478 N is applied. No engine driving force is needed.
teacher_walkthrough: Part (e): Downhill force from gravity (6278 N) exceeds resistance (1800 N) by 4478 N. Braking must provide 4.5 kN to maintain constant speed.
